topics.title: Illustrative travel advance overpayment
topics.trigger: This fictional case concerns a company travel advance partly returned by a hotel.
topics.principle: The evidence problem is separating the employee's original advance from substantiated expenses and excess amounts. The scenario does not establish an actual tax result.
topics.example: A fictional clinician receives a travel advance, cancels a hotel night and submits an expense report with the original booking total.

topics.title: Illustrative duplicate owner expense
topics.trigger: This fictional case concerns one purchase recorded through several payment systems.
topics.principle: The learning objective is tracing one underlying expenditure. A reimbursement, imported card line and vendor invoice should be connected before a reviewer evaluates the expense.
topics.example: A fictional consultant requests reimbursement for a software bill that a bookkeeper already recorded from a personal card statement.

topics.title: Illustrative shareholder distribution mismatch
topics.trigger: This fictional case compares equal cash payments with different shareholder histories.
topics.principle: The scenario illustrates why cash distributions require shareholder-level stock basis information. Debt basis and corporate cash balances do not settle the distribution analysis.
topics.example: Two fictional shareholders receive equal distributions despite different capital contributions and prior deductions.

topics.title: Illustrative shareholder debt repayment
topics.trigger: This fictional case involves an owner loan after prior-year losses.
topics.principle: The scenario separates contractual debt, payment evidence and adjusted debt basis. A bank memo stating loan repayment does not determine the shareholder's tax treatment.
topics.example: A fictional business repays its owner after using a shareholder loan to support earlier loss deductions.

topics.title: Illustrative owner compensation transition
topics.trigger: This fictional case concerns a founder who delegates operations.
topics.principle: The example distinguishes a documented role change from a salary chosen only to achieve a desired tax outcome. Actual services and compensation facts need review.
topics.example: A fictional restaurant founder hires a general manager and reduces time spent on day-to-day operations.

topics.title: Illustrative retirement census gap
topics.trigger: This fictional case concerns employee data before a proposed contribution.
topics.principle: The example shows why an owner-only estimate can be incomplete. The administrator needs accurate employment, compensation and related-employer facts.
topics.example: A fictional salon adds staff and shares an owner with another business before requesting a plan contribution estimate.

topics.title: Illustrative estimated tax revision
topics.trigger: This fictional case concerns an income forecast that changes midyear.
topics.principle: The example separates actual cash received, projected taxable income, existing payments and household withholding. It does not supply a client-specific safe-harbor conclusion.
topics.example: A fictional consulting owner receives an annual client prepayment after an earlier forecast assumed monthly billing.

topics.title: Illustrative contractor deposit timing
topics.trigger: This fictional case concerns cash received before the job is finished.
topics.principle: The evidence issue is distinguishing contract obligations, accounting treatment and usable cash. A deposit does not independently establish distributable after-tax profit.
topics.example: A fictional construction business collects a project deposit and pays materials while the work has not begun.

topics.title: Illustrative equipment installation delay
topics.trigger: This fictional case concerns equipment ordered before year-end.
topics.principle: The example separates purchase, payment, delivery and readiness for intended use. It does not assume that an invoice date determines depreciation timing.
topics.example: A fictional manufacturer pays in December, receives equipment after the holiday and completes testing in January.

topics.title: Illustrative rental closing allocation
topics.trigger: This fictional case concerns a property acquisition with several closing entries.
topics.principle: The example distinguishes land, building, financing and prepaid costs. A closing total alone is not a complete depreciable basis analysis.
topics.example: A fictional investor imports the closing statement total into the building account without reviewing lender charges or insurance.

topics.title: Illustrative phased rental renovation
topics.trigger: This fictional case concerns work completed in multiple stages.
topics.principle: The scenario shows how one final bill can conceal different projects, locations and readiness dates. Each phase needs a traceable cost and timing record.
topics.example: A fictional landlord renovates two units while keeping other units occupied and receives a consolidated contractor invoice.

topics.title: Illustrative rental owner-use calendar
topics.trigger: This fictional case concerns a property used by guests and the owner's family.
topics.principle: The scenario distinguishes personal stays, genuine repair visits and unoccupied days. A blocked calendar entry does not establish its tax classification.
topics.example: A fictional cabin owner blocks dates for family visits, maintenance and gaps between guest reservations.

topics.title: Illustrative STR service classification
topics.trigger: This fictional case concerns differing services offered to short-term guests.
topics.principle: The example focuses on actual operations rather than a listing description. Stay duration, services and participation are different factual questions.
topics.example: A fictional host offers optional daily cleaning during some stays but only turnover cleaning during others.

topics.title: Illustrative rental loss review
topics.trigger: This fictional case concerns a projected deduction that may not currently reduce other income.
topics.principle: The example distinguishes the existence of a depreciation deduction from whether a taxpayer can use the resulting loss. Separate limitation analyses can apply.
topics.example: A fictional owner receives a cost segregation estimate before supplying basis, financing and activity participation records.

topics.title: Illustrative inherited rental records
topics.trigger: This fictional case concerns a rental received through an estate.
topics.principle: The starting records differ from those of an ordinary purchase. The preparer must identify the actual transfer facts and basis before a study relies on a cost pool.
topics.example: A fictional beneficiary receives a rental and supplies only the property's current asking price to a study provider.

topics.title: Illustrative prior study overlap
topics.trigger: This fictional case concerns a property that already has a cost segregation history.
topics.principle: The example illustrates the need to identify prior classifications and later additions. A second report should not silently create a duplicate cost pool.
topics.example: A fictional owner orders another study without disclosing an earlier report and a separate furniture asset schedule.

topics.title: Illustrative refinance proceeds tracing
topics.trigger: This fictional case concerns borrowed funds used for several purposes.
topics.principle: The example separates loan security from the actual use of proceeds. Improvements, debt payoffs and personal transfers need a clear payment trail.
topics.example: A fictional rental refinance pays off debt, funds repairs and sends remaining proceeds to the owner's investment account.

topics.title: Illustrative rental sale reconciliation
topics.trigger: This fictional case concerns a sale after improvements and depreciation changes.
topics.principle: The example separates sale proceeds, debt payoff, selling costs and asset basis history. The owner's net cash at closing is not the same as taxable gain.
topics.example: A fictional investor sells a furnished rental after replacing appliances and implementing an earlier study.

topics.title: Illustrative adviser transition gaps
topics.trigger: This fictional case concerns a new professional inheriting incomplete records.
topics.principle: The example shows why prior returns alone may not explain elections, workpapers and unresolved issues. A transition file should identify what remains unknown.
topics.example: A fictional owner changes advisers and supplies return PDFs while shareholder basis and asset history remain with the former firm.

topics.title: Illustrative tax proposal comparison
topics.trigger: This fictional case concerns two packages that use similar marketing language.
topics.principle: The example compares deliverables, responsibilities and total costs without creating a provider ranking. It does not claim that either proposal produced a real client result.
topics.example: A fictional buyer compares a planning-only fee with a package including limited return preparation and ongoing reviews.
